articles.title: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia’s new interim CEO?
articles.summary: For 13 years, Colette Kress helped manage the company’s transformation from a graphics-chip maker into the company at the center of the AI boom.
articles.body: For 13 years, Colette Kress helped manage the company’s transformation from a graphics-chip maker into the company at the center of the artificial intelligence boom. Now, she’s being asked to lead it through one of the most turbulent moments in its history. Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, was named interim CEO Thursday following the abrupt resignation of Jensen Huang, who co-founded the company and led it for 33 years. Huang’s departure comes amid revelations of extramarital relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and one of his own reports. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead,” Kress said in a press release. “Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” “I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy,” Kress said in an email to staff following her appointment, acknowledging the “extraordinarily difficult period” for the company. Kress joined the company in September 2013 after tenures at Cisco and Microsoft, where she also held finance positions. She has helped see Nvidia through its transition from a video game-focused processor manufacturer to an AI-chip powerhouse. “Having worked with Colette at Cisco, I know she understands what it takes to lead through major market transitions, build strong teams, and execute at scale,” said John Chambers, former Cisco executive chairman and CEO. “Nvidia is at a critical moment, not just for the company, but for the future of AI and America’s technology leadership. I really believe Colette’s ability to step in as interim CEO. She is an amazing leader.” Chambers said that despite the uncertainty a leadership change creates, he does not believe it will fundamentally alter the company’s trajectory. “Every company goes through near death experiences,” Chambers said. “Nvidia is no different. It will be a challenging next year, I think they will continue to be a leading force in the AI landscape.” Kress and Huang worked closely together. Huang long leaned on Kress during financial conferences and the company’s earnings calls to debrief the investing public about the latest developments with the company’s operations. The company’s release noted its planned earnings call will go ahead on Nov. 17. Kress is expected to lead it, five days after taking on the new role. As Nvidia grew its business to focus on AI, Kress has been instrumental in managing financial relationships. Under her watch, the company has invested heavily into the technology sector, including Intel, Nokia and a partnership with OpenAI. In the past, Kress has noted that the inability to sell to China would affect the industry in the long run, a stance echoing Huang’s. “If you are unable to sell products to them, it will have an impact,” she said in an interview to Israeli publication Globes. In a November 2025 earnings call, Kress told investors the company is not expecting data center compute revenue from China. “Sizable purchase orders never materialized in the quarter due to geopolitical issues and the increasingly competitive market in China,” Kress told investors, according to a transcript of the call. “While we were disappointed in the current state that prevents us from shipping more competitive Data Center compute products to China, we are committed to continued engagement with the U.S. and China governments and will continue to advocate for America’s ability to compete around the world.” Kress’ tenure at Nvidia has been lucrative. Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index named her as one of two new Nvidia executives whose net worth exceeded $1 billion last year, largely based on the company stock she holds. Nvidia shares dipped Thursday following the announcement of Huang’s resignation and Kress’ new position. The crisis comes at a pivotal moment for AI development in the U.S. as outfits like Anthropic and OpenAI rely on Nvidia’s dominant chip technology. Kress’ role will be to see the company through the crisis and again cast it as a reliable player in the global markets. That may be difficult, as both investors and lawmakers are probing Nvidia for details of the alleged spy plot. Huang has agreed to brief Congress on his relationship as well as the company’s security protocols. “Jensen Huang’s decision to resign from NVIDIA does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement Thursday. “They still owe Congress answers.”

articles.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: The attack is thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an open stretch of the Baltic Sea.
articles.body:
Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.

Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.

The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.

Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.

Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.

The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.

Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.

Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.

Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."

The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.

"The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.

Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.

Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.

Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace.

He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.

Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.

Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".

articles.title: Regional security dominates European talks in Dublin amid hybrid attacks
articles.summary: European nations discuss security collaboration and an envoy for Ukraine peace talks during the summit in Ireland.
articles.body:
Leaders from more than 40 European countries have gathered in Dublin for a summit dominated by the growing number of hybrid attacks across the continent.

The biannual European Political Community (EPC), a regional group established in 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine , brought together heads of state and government officials on Thursday to discuss the region’s fragile security, amid a new United States-backed effort to revive talks between Russia and Ukraine to end the war.

The gathering comes after a series of hoaxes and cyberattacks that have recently targeted supermarkets, blood banks, passenger airlines, schools and media outlets in Europe.

Earlier on Thursday, more than 3,700 Italian schools received hoax bomb warnings , a day after 6,300 schools were affected by a similar widespread alert .

The Republic of Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheal Martin, known as the taoiseach, said those responsible for the attacks seek to “create confusion, sow division and weaken public confidence in our democratic systems”.

“We will not allow them to succeed. We will continue to use forums like this to share our experiences, learn from one another and to work together to protect our democracies,” he told reporters.

A major topic of conversation was Europe’s quest for an envoy to represent it in peace talks after calls from Washington and Kyiv. It remains unclear who will be named as European representative.

Earlier on Thursday, US envoy Steve Witkoff said Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine discussions following a meeting in Moscow .

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged his “complete support” to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and said he would push for European representation in the US-brokered talks.

Burnham co-chaired a group meeting on Ukraine with Zelenskyy at the summit.

The EPC comes at a moment of growing political tensions in Europe, and a week after the US midterm elections that saw extensive losses for US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.

While populist leaders have recently been ousted in Serbia and in Hungary , the far right is still on the rise in Europe and has made recent gains in regional elections in Germany. Voters will cast their ballots in the months ahead in the continent’s biggest countries, including Spain, France, Italy and Poland.

articles.title: Microsoft struggling to restore service as global outage affects Outlook and Teams
articles.summary: Services including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's AI software Copilot have been affected by "connectivity problems".
articles.body:
Microsoft is struggling to fix a global outage of its service that is reportedly affecting tens of thousands of users.

Services including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's AI software Copilot have been affected by "connectivity problems".

"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," the company wrote on X.

Reports of problems with Outlook peaked globally at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT on Thursday, according to monitoring website Downdetector.

The company said it had been able to restore part of its service, but about an hour later, it gave another update saying those servers "can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic".

While the issue was originally reported in the US, Microsoft said users "in any region" may be affected.

The company said it had found some of its infrastructure was "experiencing elevated load across multiple regions" which was "likely contributing to the connectivity errors".

It later gave an update that the extra load was probably caused by several servers being "unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure".

OpenAI said it was investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors in which new connections may be broken and tools are not working as expected.

Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider affecting its Microsoft 365 connector.

Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted the tech giant's suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide.

Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on 12 November, rescheduled it to 16 November citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage.

articles.title: A man sued his former fiancée for $120,000 and the return of his $5,300 engagement ring after their eight-year relationship ended; a New York court rejected his claims
articles.summary: A New York court has rejected a man's demand for the return of his engagement ring and $120,000 in damages after his eight-year relationship with his
articles.body: A New York court has rejected a man's demand for the return of his engagement ring and $120,000 in damages after his eight-year relationship with his former fiancée ended following a domestic dispute. Jason Dieterle sued Heather M. Lynch, seeking compensation for alleged home improvements and money from a joint bank account, along with the ring or $5,300 to cover its cost. However, in a January 30, 2026, ruling, the Supreme Court of Erie County dismissed his claims, finding insufficient evidence for the financial demands and ruling that his own conduct barred him from recovering the engagement ring.Why did the man demand his engagement ring and $120,000According to the court's decision, Dieterle and Heather M. Lynch had been together and engaged for approximately eight years. During the relationship, the couple moved into Lynch's recently purchased house in Akron, New York, along with Dieterle's two children. The property was registered in Lynch's name, and she was responsible for paying the mortgage. Around the same time, Dieterle added Lynch as a joint account holder to his bank account, which contained approximately $40,000 from the recent sale of his home.Both parties used the account for different expenses. Dieterle used the money to pay personal debts, loans from his parents and child support, while Lynch used it for household groceries, petrol and holiday gifts. Although both knew about each other's withdrawals, they later disagreed over whether either party had withdrawn more than their fair share.The relationship ended on October 8, 2023, following a domestic dispute. According to the Village of Akron police report, officers arrived at the property and found Lynch standing in the driveway with blood on her shirt. Dieterle's 74-year-old father was also present, with several facial lacerations. The report stated that Lynch and Dieterle's father alleged that Dieterle had been in an uncontrolled rage, which they attributed to alcohol and drug use earlier that day. Following an altercation, police arrested Dieterle and transported him to the Erie County Medical Centre.The court also recorded that Dieterle had been convicted of various charges in Newstead Town Court and that Lynch subsequently obtained an order of protection against him for two years. The engagement ended on the day of the incident. Dieterle removed his belongings from the property and purchased another house in the same town.Why did Dieterle demand $120,000 from his former fiancéeLess than a year after the engagement ended, Dieterle filed a lawsuit seeking financial compensation from Lynch. According to the judgment, his claims included $80,000 for repairs and improvements he said he had carried out on her property over the preceding four years, approximately $40,000 that had previously been held in their joint bank account, and the return of his engagement ring or $5,300 to cover its cost.In his affidavit, Dieterle listed several services he claimed to have performed while living at the property. These included landscaping, seeding, removing trees and stumps, garden maintenance, window restoration, garage restoration, painting and fireplace restoration. He also claimed to have repaired the living room and kitchen ceilings, installed lighting and dining room flooring, restored the staircase and carried out bathroom, plumbing and wardrobe repairs.However, the court found that he had not provided supporting documentation for these claims. Justice Weinmann noted that Dieterle had submitted no receipts, invoices, timesheets or other records establishing the work performed or its value. The judgment specifically questioned the basis of his financial demands, stating that "The claim for $60,000 appears to be pulled out of thin air." The court also noted that there was no evidence that Dieterle had been a general contractor, repairman or handyman.Why did the court reject Dieterle's $40,000 bank account claimThe dispute over the joint bank account was another important part of the case. Dieterle sought to recover approximately $40,000 that had originally come from the sale of his previous home. However, the court examined the bank documentation and found that Lynch had been added as a joint owner with a right of survivorship.The judgment referred to Section 675 of New York Banking Law, which provides that funds in a joint account with a right of survivorship belong to both account holders as joint tenants. Under this arrangement, either account holder can access the funds during their lifetimes. The court distinguished this from a convenience account, in which the additional account holder does not acquire ownership of the deposited funds.Justice Weinmann concluded that Lynch had every legal right to use the account, including for her own expenses, because Dieterle had voluntarily added her as a joint owner. The court also observed that both parties had used the account individually and jointly. It therefore found that Dieterle had no valid claim of unjust enrichment based on the alleged imbalance in their withdrawals.The court also rejected his claims for unjust enrichment and quantum meruit concerning the home improvements. To establish unjust enrichment, a claimant must show that the other party received a benefit at their expense and that allowing the other party to retain it would be against equity and good conscience. For quantum meruit, a claimant must establish that services were performed in good faith, accepted by the other party, provided with an expectation of payment and had a reasonable value. The court found that Dieterle had failed to establish the necessary elements of these claims.What does New York law say about returning engagement ringsThe engagement ring was the final issue considered in the judgment. Under Section 80-b of New York Civil Rights Law, a person who gives property, including an engagement ring, in contemplation of marriage may generally seek its return if the marriage does not take place. The law was revised in 1965 to address disputes involving broken engagements.The court referred to the 1971 Court of Appeals decision in Gaden v. Gaden, which established that the return of engagement gifts should not depend on determining which party was at fault for the failed relationship. The purpose of the legislation, as explained in that earlier ruling, was to return the parties to their positions before the engagement without rewarding or punishing either person for the marriage not taking place.However, Justice Weinmann also considered the legal doctrine of unclean hands. This equitable principle can prevent a person from obtaining relief from a court when their own wrongful or unconscionable conduct is directly connected to the matter being disputed and has injured the other party. The judgment referred to earlier decisions, including Lowe v. Quinn and Levy v. Braverman, while examining how the principle applied to the engagement ring dispute.Applying the doctrine, the judge found that Dieterle's actions had brought the engagement to an end. The decision stated that his assault on his former fiancée constituted "immoral and unconscionable conduct". It further concluded that he could not seek an equitable remedy for the return of the ring after his own actions had caused the engagement to end.The judge wrote: "He alone was responsible." The decision concluded that Dieterle had "both figuratively and literally—unclean hands" and should not be allowed to profit from his own actions. The court consequently ruled that the engagement ring did not have to be returned to him.The January 30, 2026, decision rejected Dieterle's claims, and defence counsel was directed to submit an order to the court within 30 days of the decision's entry.You use AI every day. articles.title: A fake fundraising website showed $16,000 collected for a 13-year-old Atlanta boy's funeral; his family said it never received the money, and a funeral director stepped in to cover the costs
articles.summary: A grieving Atlanta family faced an unexpected financial struggle after the death of their 13-year-old son, Mason Towler, when fundraising campaigns
articles.body: A grieving Atlanta family faced an unexpected financial struggle after the death of their 13-year-old son, Mason Towler, when fundraising campaigns created in his name failed to provide the money needed for his funeral. A separate website later displayed $16,000 in donations linked to the boy's death, but his family said it never received those funds. According to Atlanta News First, the ordeal involved unauthorised fundraising efforts, a suspected copycat website and weeks of uncertainty over funeral arrangements before a local funeral director stepped in to cover the costs.How did a fake fundraising website show $16,000 for Mason Towler's funeralThe online fundraising dispute followed the death of Mason Towler, who was killed on 29 January 2026 after wandering from his home and entering traffic on Interstate 75 near Cleveland Avenue in Atlanta. A pickup truck struck the 13-year-old, who had autism, leaving his parents, Salena Holmes and DeMarko Towler, facing the loss of their child and the challenge of arranging his funeral.According to Atlanta News First, a family friend connected Holmes with Renee Sunshine Lewis, a community leader and bereavement advocate who offered to help raise money for Mason's funeral. Lewis requested photographs and sent Holmes an agreement seeking permission to launch a GoFundMe campaign and contact the media.Holmes declined the proposal, with text messages confirming that she had not authorised the fundraising effort.Despite the refusal, Lewis created two GoFundMe campaigns connected to Mason, according to a spokesperson for the platform. Both were subsequently removed for violating its rules against fraudulent or misleading fundraising activities.The original campaigns failed to provide funeral assistanceThe two campaigns created by Lewis reportedly collected just $175 before being removed. However, the money never reached Mason's family.Atlanta News First reported that GoFundMe confirmed the donations had been refunded to their original contributors. The platform's spokesperson said the refunds covered the entire $175 raised through those campaigns.The fundraising attempts therefore provided no financial assistance to Holmes and Towler, who were still trying to arrange a funeral for their son.The news organisation also attempted to contact Lewis for an explanation. Her telephone number was called multiple times, but one attempt ended with the call being disconnected. She did not respond to text messages or Facebook messages sent by the investigative team.State records cited by Atlanta News First showed that Lewis' bereavement business, Gracy & Mercy Concierge Bereavement Services, had been dissolved in 2017.A separate website displayed donations the family could not traceWith no money available from the earlier campaigns, Holmes faced the possibility of handing her son's body over to the county for cremation. She eventually created her own GoFundMe fundraiser, which collected $700, according to Atlanta News First.The investigation then uncovered another troubling development. Information and photographs from both Holmes' campaign and the earlier campaigns created by Lewis appeared on GoFundRaiser.org, a separate website that was not affiliated with GoFundMe.The two pages featuring Mason's story displayed a combined total of $16,000 in donations. However, the family said it had never received the money, and there was no clear explanation of where the displayed funds had gone.Atlanta News First reported that the origins of the information on GoFundRaiser.org remained unclear. The website had reportedly reposted photographs and personal stories from legitimate fundraising campaigns without permission, according to news reports and dozens of consumer complaints cited by the investigation. Following the Atlanta News First investigation, GoFundRaiser.org blocked access to its website.How did a funeral director help the family at its lowest pointWhile the fundraising dispute continued, Mason's body remained at Stocks Funeral Home Kirkwood Chapel in Atlanta for nearly a month. His parents were still waiting to give their son a funeral, despite the money displayed online in connection with his death.The situation changed when Kyle Stocks, who had taken over the family funeral business the previous year, decided to intervene.According to Atlanta News First, Stocks covered the entire cost of Mason's arrangements, including his cremation, funeral service and obituary. His decision meant the family could finally proceed without having to find additional money to meet the expenses.DeMarko Towler described the assistance as a significant relief, saying his son would be able to leave in the right way.Stocks' decision stood in contrast to the unsuccessful fundraising efforts that had left the family struggling. Rather than relying on the money displayed on an unrelated website, the funeral director provided the practical assistance that the parents needed to arrange their son's farewell.The investigation did not establish where the $16,000 displayed on GoFundRaiser.org had gone, leaving the discrepancy unresolved.What precautions can donors take before contributing onlineThe case also highlighted the risks associated with online fundraising, particularly when people donate in response to stories involving bereaved families or urgent financial needs.Atlanta News First outlined several precautions recommended by consumer advocates to help donors avoid misleading campaigns.These include using established fundraising platforms, checking whether a website closely resembles a legitimate service and verifying the identity of the person organising a campaign. Donors are also advised to examine domain ownership, search for the organiser's name and check public business records for information about associated organisations.The Federal Trade Commission recommends reverse image searches to determine whether photographs used in a fundraising campaign appear elsewhere online. Searching for the person's name and details of the reported incident can also help establish whether the campaign is genuine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: We spent months testing Tower 28’s viral skin care and makeup— here’s what is actually worth buying
articles.summary: We tried Tower 28’s skin care and beauty lines, including cleansers, sunscreens, lip balm and more, to see how they stack up.
articles.body: If you’ve heard of hypochlorous acid spray, you’re likely familiar with Tower 28 Beauty’s viral SOS Spray, which is a summer skin care mainstay among our NBC Selected editors. While a few of us have tried (and loved) some of Tower 28’s products here and there, we were curious about the rest of the lineup — so we decided to put them to the test. To see if they live up to the spray’s hype, four NBC Selected editors tested some of the brand’s most popular products for over two months. Our verdict: Tower 28 makes some excellent everyday staples, particularly if you prefer lightweight, natural-looking makeup, but not everything impressed us equally. Below is a breakdown of what we’d buy again, what we’d skip and who we think the brand is best for. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Our honest review of Tower 28 Beauty Best skin care products we tested This is one of the most popular hypochlorous acid sprays available and frankly, it’s not hard to see why. I use it as a toner in between my cleanser and serums, and I love that the fine mist soothes my skin, particularly after I use an exfoliating cleanser (which is business as usual for my acne-prone skin). I also like bringing it to the beach because the fine mist feels cooling and refreshing in hotter weather, plus soothes irritation after a long day in the sun (just make sure you use an SPF, too). I’ll admit, I was definitely skeptical about this cleanser at first. I didn’t really have any expectations; I figured it would just be a run of the mill face wash that I’d switch off after I finished testing. However, I ended up really loving this wash. Not only does it leave my skin feeling comfortable rather than tight after washing, but I also noticed that some of my post-acne marks looked less noticeable over the course of testing. My favorite part, though, is how well it removes my eye makeup. I usually have to use an oil-based cleanser to take off my mascara and eyeshadow, but this cleanser removes it in one go without me having to tug or pull at my skin. NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio, who has dry, sensitive skin that’s prone to rosacea, usually tends to avoid full-coverage foundations since they can break her out. However, since trying this tinted sunscreen for the first time a few years ago, it’s been a staple in her routine. “It has the perfect serum consistency, so it doesn’t feel heavy or sticky in the slightest,” she says. “It also has enough coverage to even out my skin tone and cover up my redness, which means I can use it on its own without any other makeup,” she says. However, don’t expect it to give you full coverage: “I usually wear a heavier foundation when I’m going out for the night or want to cover any acne or dark spots,” says Godio. The packaging is on the smaller side, but the tip is a plus for our testers. “It has a thin, needle-nose tip, so it doesn’t get everywhere when I apply it,” says Godio. Although the shade range isn’t as extensive as the Swipe Serum products (more on those below), the tinted sunscreen does have broad-spectrum SPF 30 protection, making it a great lightweight option for warmer days. Best makeup products we tested Everyone on the NBC Selected staff knows by now that I’m a huge hoarder of lip products, including glosses, oils and balms. That’s why you should trust me when I say that this is one of the best gloss formulas I’ve tried. It’s hydrating, non-sticky and I especially love how long it lasts on my lips. I’m a chronic reapplier regardless, but it was nice to know that with this lip jelly, it wasn’t necessary to do it as often. The shades also have a great color payoff, so you can wear it alone, or pair it with a lip liner. The shades come in a range of nudes to suit different skin tones, so it’s easy to wear with nothing but a fresh face. Godio has this lip oil in multiple shades, and says she keeps them in every bag she owns. “It gives the perfect pop of color without feeling too heavy or sticky, and the texture is so smooth and buttery,” she says. She also likes that it keeps her lips from feeling dry even during the wintertime. Godio is also a fan of the brand’s other lippie, the Lip Softie, which is extremely lightweight, hydrating and gives the perfect sheer tint, she says. In my opinion, this foundation is perfect for everyday wear: It doesn’t feel heavy on the skin and blends well enough to give you a glowy, very natural finish. I also liked wearing it for shorter periods of time, like when I’m running errands or going to lunch with a friend. However, after a few hours, the oiliness from my skin would seep through. NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown says the foundation feels extremely lightweight, but the coverage is a little lighter than she prefers. We both agree that you’ll need something heavier or more buildable to cover dark spots and blemishes. The foundation also has the brand’s widest shade range yet, with 36 total options across light, medium and dark/deep shades, along with warm, neutral and pink/red undertones. Since the range is so extensive, I was able to find a perfect shade match right off the bat (something that I’ve struggled with while using other foundations). NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack doesn’t usually wear concealer, but says this product made her want to start wearing one consistently. “The formula is super lightweight, doesn’t crease at all under my eyes and blends seamlessly with the rest of my makeup,” she says. “It immediately brightens my under eyes and completely covers my dark circles.” When I used this concealer to cover my dark circles, I noticed the lightweight texture didn’t crease underneath my eyes. However, it did look slightly greasy and shiny after I’d worn it for a few hours. Like the foundation, it also has a wide shade range, although it’s available in only 28 shades, compared to the foundation’s 36. I only ever use smudge-resistant mascaras, since I’m prone to touching my face and eyes. I thought I’d officially found the one with Essence’s Lash Without Limits Tubing Mascara, but this Tower 28 mascara definitely shook things up for me.The brush has a curved handle and spaced bristles that help to separate the lashes and prevent them from clumping. Cusask, who’s been using the same mascara since middle school, felt similarly: “This mascara from Tower 28 is the first one I’ve tried that’s made me want to ditch my tried-and-true mascara,” she says. “My biggest issue with mascaras I’ve tried in the past is that they made my lashes stick together, so it looks like I have four big eyelashes (which is not a cute look). This helps them look so much fuller and darker.” As a fellow oily skin girl, Cusack’s biggest pet peeve is when her makeup seems to melt off her face soon after applying it. So, she’s always on the lookout for pigmented products with a lot of staying power, and this blush checks off all her boxes. “It’s super pigmented, and the matte powder keeps the extra oil on my cheeks at bay,” she says. We also both like that you really don’t need much product to get the full color payoff. “It’s a perfect example of a little goes a long way — I only need to tap my brush a couple times and my cheeks become a perfectly rosy pink,” says Cusack. The blush comes in seven core shades, most of which are varying tones of pink or nude, along with two brighter, limited-edition shades with red and orange bases. However, be sure to handle your blush with care; after dropping one of mine, the powder cracked and partially broke (but that hasn’t stopped me from using it afterward). I love using a cream blush as a base before a blush powder, and this one layers perfectly with any powder product I use. Cusack has always preferred a cream blush over powder, and says this one solidified that choice for her. “The texture is incredibly smooth and it practically melts into my skin,” she says. The blush (like many of Tower 28’s products) also comes in a wide shade range, which is great for somebody like me who likes to try different color combinations with my blush and eye makeup. Most of the colors are also great for everyday wear: “The Happy Hour shade is one of the best I’ve ever tried on my fair skin and makes me look like I have a perfect, natural flush,” says Cusack. Shimmer eye products are usually a hit or miss for me; they’re usually flaky, chunky or don’t stay on long enough. However, this eyeshadow stick did none of the above. The water-based formula is smooth and feels cooling on my lids. Although I did swipe it directly onto my eyes a few times, I preferred applying it by dipping my makeup brushes onto the top. Since the product is so pigmented, it showed up just as well, and this made it easier to blend out with other shadows. Godio is also a fan of this eyeshadow stick, which she wears when going out on the weekends. “I love a pop of shimmer when I go out to dinner or dancing with friends, and I usually reach for this eyeshadow to complete my eye look,” she says. “I have the bright purple color, which is even more fun to use. I love how easily it blends into my lids and works with both cream and powder eyeshadows underneath.” What to know before buying Tower 28 Overall, we think Tower 28 lives up to the hype. However, there are a few things that, in our experience, can improved: Mid-range pricing: I wouldn’t exactly describe Tower 28’s prices as expensive, but they’re not exactly affordable. While the lip products start at $16, the complexion products hover closer to the $30 mark, making it pricier than drugstore alternatives, especially for skin care products you may have to replace more often.Some complexion products may look shiny on oily skin: Though the blushes held up well during testing, the complexion products weren’t our favorites for oily skin. After a few hours of wearing these products, our oily skin testers experienced separation, greasiness and shine. If you have oily skin, you may want to pair them with setting powder or wear them for shorter periods of time.Intense sensation on the ShineOn Plumping Jelly Lip Oil: Although we loved most of the Tower 28 lippies we tried, we didn’t feel the same about the ShineOn Plumping Jelly Lip Oil. Although the formula is lightweight and hydrating, the tingling, plumping sensation is very strong, to the point where our testers felt it on their tongue if it touched their lips even slightly. Some testers found it fairly uncomfortable to wear, especially those with sensitive skin or lips. How we tested Tower 28 Beauty Four NBC Selected editors tested Tower 28’s makeup and skin care lines for two months, although many of us were already familiar with the brand’s offerings and have been using them for years. We included skin care like cleansers and toners in our testing pool, along with beauty products like lip oils, blushes, foundations and concealers. While testing, each editor paid special attention to how the products worked with their specific skin type and needs. We also kept these factors in mind: Efficacy: Does the product perform as advertised? Does it address the issues it’s designed to?Ease of use: Is it easy to apply? Are the instructions clear and easy to follow?Packaging: Is the packaging travel-friendly? Does it come in a tube, jar, wand, pump etc.? Is an applicator included?Pricing: Does the product feel worth the money? Is this something you would repurchase on your own? Who is Tower 28 Beauty for? Tower 28 is best for people who prefer lightweight makeup with natural-looking finishes, particularly those with sensitive or reactive skin. The products are beginner-friendly and easy to apply, and experienced makeup users who prefer sheer, everyday formulas will also find plenty to like. However, if you prefer a lot of coverage, have extremely oily skin or primarily shop at drugstore price points, the brand may be less appealing. One of the biggest standouts from Tower 28’s skin care line is that it’s great for people with sensitive skin due to its gentle, anti-inflammatory ingredients. Many Tower 28 products have received the National Eczema Association’s Seal of Acceptance, which identifies products suitable for people with eczema or sensitive skin. The Swipe Serum Foundation is among them, making it one of the first foundations to get the designation, according to the brand. If price is a concern, there are some meaningful alternatives available. For example, I like the Magic Molecule Hypochlorous Acid Spray (which comes in at $17.99 compared to Tower 28’s $28 spray), the Essence Lash Without Limits Tubing Mascara ($4.97) and Maybelline’s Cheek Heat ($9.99) for a natural, rosy color on my cheeks. While those picks aren’t necessarily identical to Tower 28’s formulas or finishes, they’re worth considering if the brand’s mid-range prices are more than you want to spend. Why trust NBC Selected? articles.title: Using an AI agent to buy your flights? This airline is banning them from booking on your behalf.
articles.summary: Booking with an AI agent may seem convenient and potentially cost-saving, but consumer advocates say it's not the best approach for protecting your travel pl...
articles.body:
United Airlines is restricting how customers can use AI to book their flights, the company announced on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The airline stated that protecting travelers' privacy and data was the reason for the decision.

In a statement, United said that sharing account credentials with "personal, third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles."

It also noted that automated AI actions may violate Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation regulations, citing, for example, the requirement that travelers acknowledge their bags do not contain "banned substances like explosives" — something an AI agent cannot legally confirm.

"As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants," the airline said.

United also updated its Digital Trust Center to include further details on how travelers should and should not use AI agents when planning travel. The airline told Travel Weekly it will honor any bookings made with an AI agent before Nov. 11.

United isn't the only airline responding to the uptick in AI agent flight bookings.

Other airlines, however, are aware that customers are using these agents to book their flights. JetBlue president Marty St. George said on Nov. 11 that he's aware customers are booking with AI agents and that, while it may lead to additional costs for the airline, he believes it should adapt, Reuters reported.

Delta's policy states that while customers may use third-party agents if they so choose, they remain responsible for what the AI agent does. So, if your AI agent books you on a nonrefundable trip to Australia when you actually intended to book a flight to Austria — well, you're on your own to sort out the mess. And Delta also has the right to block or reject agents or transactions on its website.

A representative for American Airlines told Fast Company that while some AI tools can facilitate the purchase of American Airlines tickets, the airline actively monitors traffic across their website ​and app, and "can investigate, manage ​or block automated traffic when necessary ​to protect our ​customers and their experience."

In October, Southwest launched a ChatGPT plug-in that helps customers shop for flights, though they must complete booking themselves on the Southwest website.

Why you should be careful booking travel with an AI agent — even if you're allowed

Booking a flight with AI may seem like a way to offload a task, or even potentially save money if an AI agent is able to comb through the lowest-priced flights for your route more efficiently than you can. However, consumer advocates tell Yahoo Travel that it's best to avoid booking a flight with an AI agent, regardless of the airline.

"AI agents still make mistakes," Christopher Elliott, a consumer advocate and founder of The Elliott Report , tells Yahoo Travel. "They can book the wrong dates or misread a fare rule. When that happens, the airline will tell you the error is yours, and good luck getting a refund from a bot."

But Elliott says he's worried it will be hard for airlines to enforce this rule. "United's updated contract of carriage lets it cancel a reservation made or changed by an AI agent. A passenger who books through a travel site that uses one of these tools, possibly without knowing it, could get to the airport and find no seat. That's a much bigger risk than any booking error a bot is likely to make."

If you don't want to make a reservation yourself, Michelle Couch-Friedman, founder of consumer advocacy website and organization Consumer Rescue , tells Yahoo Travel it's best to rely on a travel adviser instead. "Professional travel advisers typically carry errors and omissions insurance to protect against mistakes — AI does not," she says.

articles.title: Chick-fil-A customers have days left to order cult favorite sandwich before it vanishes
articles.summary: Chicken & Waffles exit most Chick-fil-A menus on Nov. 14, but Tampa, Chicago and Raleigh diners can still order expanded waffle breakfast options.
articles.body: Chick-fil-A is pulling a seasonal favorite from its menus, but some lucky diners in certain cities may still have a chance to order it. The chain's Chicken & Waffles sandwiches are leaving most menus on Nov. 14, or while supplies last, but select restaurants in Tampa, Chicago and Raleigh will keep serving a breakfast version as the chain tests four additional waffle sandwiches. The nationwide limited-time offering debuted in August after a test run in 2025, pairing the chain's chicken filet with maple-flavored waffles, applewood smoked bacon, honey butter spread and syrup. MCDONALD'S MCRIB RETURNS FOR LIMITED TIME, BUT CUSTOMERS IN SOME CITIES WILL MISS OUT "We've loved seeing how much our guests enjoyed Chicken & Waffles this fall, especially the breakfast sandwich," Allison Duncan, Chick-fil-A's director of menu and packaging, told QSR. But beginning Nov. 16, participating restaurants in the three cities will offer the Chicken & Waffles Breakfast Sandwich with an Original, Spicy or Grilled filet, along with Chicken, Egg & Cheese; Bacon, Egg & Cheese; Sausage, Egg & Cheese; and Grilled Chicken, Bacon, Egg & Cheese waffle sandwiches. The test menu will be available during breakfast hours, until 10:30 a.m. POPEYES BRINGS BACK POPULAR MENU ITEM FOR GOOD, AND NOT EVERYONE IS HAPPY Chick-fil-A selects test markets based on opportunities to gather feedback from customers and local owner-operators, the company told Fox News Digital. The company did not identify participating restaurants but said individual locations typically share test menu details on their social media pages. Customers in the test cities can also check the Chick-fil-A app to see whether their local restaurant is participating. CHICK-FIL-A'S FIRST NEW SAUCE IN 10 YEARS HAS FANS SHARING STRONG REACTION Duncan said the company hopes the test will help it learn what customers want next. Chick-fil-A has not announced whether the expanded menu could come to more locations. Online, fans are mourning the nationwide exit. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES But others don't mind seeing the item go. Some Reddit users said the waffles were too dense or not soft enough to soak up the syrup, while others said they were excited that the limited-time item was making room for something new. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The chicken and waffles were part of a yearlong "Newstalgia"-inspired celebration, which the company said offered "a delicious twist on familiar favorites." Along with it came a s'mores milkshake and frosted coffee lineup, which are also ending on Nov. 14. It includes a new Peppermint Cream Cold Brew, returning peppermint drinks and Chicken Tortilla Soup, along with Spicy Chick-fil-A Sauce, which is joining the nationwide menu permanently, Fox News Digital reported last month.

articles.title: An Oklahoma homeowner hosted 141 guests during 36 short-term stays despite neighbourhood rules; after a lower appeals court lifted restrictions, the state Supreme Court restored the ban and upheld $8,528 in fines
articles.summary: An Oklahoma homeowner has been ordered to pay more than $8,000 after the state Supreme Court restored a neighbourhood ban on short-term property rentals.
articles.body: An Oklahoma homeowner has been ordered to pay more than $8,000 after the state Supreme Court restored a neighbourhood ban on short-term property rentals. The ruling ends a lengthy legal dispute over rules governing how homes can be used in a residential community. According to the court's decision published by Justia, the case of Silverhawk Homeowners Association, Inc. v. Tawose focused on whether neighbourhood rules designed to protect residential areas could prevent homeowners from running businesses similar to hotels. The homeowner, identified as Adewale Eniola Tawose in the Oklahoma Supreme Court's final ruling in case 122129, hosted 141 guests across 36 short-term stays at his property in the Silverhawk subdivision between late 2021 and late 2023. The exact location of the subdivision was not clearly identified in the court's case summary. However, the dispute reflects wider efforts by homeowners associations to enforce rules against short-term rental businesses.The case reached its conclusion on November 10, 2026, when the Oklahoma Supreme Court overturned an earlier decision by the Court of Civil Appeals and restored the neighbourhood's restrictions. The justices upheld the original decision of the District Court of Oklahoma County, ordering Tawose to pay $8,528 in fines and assessments allowed under the association's rules.Neighbourhood covenants versus commercial operationsThe main disagreement involved the meaning of the neighbourhood's Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions. Homeowners associations such as Silverhawk HOA create these rules to control how properties are used, protect home values and maintain a peaceful living environment. These private agreements often require properties to be used only as homes and may restrict business activities within the neighbourhood. According to Justia's report on the case, Silverhawk Homeowners Association argued that regularly renting out a property for short stays, often just a few days, was a violation of these rules. The Supreme Court's opinion explains how the association tried to enforce its restrictions. The HOA Board contacted several homeowners it believed were breaking the short-term rental rules and asked them to stop. Two owners agreed and changed their properties to long-term rentals. Tawose refused, arguing that he had the right to use his property as he wished.Differing interpretations by the courtsThe legal dispute went through several stages in Oklahoma's court system. Initially, the District Court ruled in favour of the homeowners association. After a five-day trial, the judge ordered Tawose to stop running the short-term rental business and pay $8,528 in fines and assessments that had built up under the association's rules. Tawose appealed the decision to the Oklahoma Court of Civil Appeals. The appeals court agreed with some of his arguments and overturned parts of the lower court's ruling. It found that short-term rentals did not necessarily change the residential nature of a property and could be similar to having guests stay there. The court also considered the argument that receiving rent did not automatically turn the property's use into a commercial business under the wording of the Silverhawk agreement. Following this decision, Silverhawk Homeowners Association asked the Oklahoma Supreme Court to review the case and provide a final ruling on the dispute.Supreme Court final judgment on property useThe Oklahoma Supreme Court rejected the Court of Civil Appeals' decision and upheld the residential restrictions. When examining Tawose's rental activities, the justices pointed to several details that made the operation more like a hotel or motel than an ordinary home. According to the court's findings reported by Justia, the property had set check-in and check-out times, and Tawose supplied basic items to guests. The court also considered evidence about cleaning services between stays and the role of a cleaner who helped manage the property and respond to guest questions. Tawose disputed some of this evidence. The court also noted that Tawose had retained the right to enter the property, similar to a hotel or motel operator. It found that the property was being offered to paying guests in a way that resembled a hospitality business.The final ruling concluded that regularly renting the property for profit in a hotel-like manner went against the purpose of the neighbourhood's residential rules. The 141 guests who stayed at the property over 36 separate visits also made the arrangement different from a traditional long-term rental, even though guests lived in the home during their stays. As a result, the Supreme Court restored the original District Court decision. It reinstated the ban on Tawose's short-term rental business and upheld the $8,528 in fines and assessments imposed against him.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sewage spills in Scotland: Has your local river or sea been polluted?
articles.summary: More than 76,000 sewage spills were recorded at overflow sites previously unmonitored by Scottish Water, BBC Scotland News analysis has found.
articles.body:
More than 76,000 sewage spills were recorded after new monitoring equipment was installed at waste overflow sites in Scotland, BBC analysis suggests.

The addition of 1,009 sewer monitors in 2024 increased the proportion of the Scottish Water network being monitored from 6% to 30%.

Now the latest figures have revealed tens of thousands of spills which would previously have been unrecorded, including hundreds at beauty spots like Loch Lomond.

Scottish Water said the vast majority of the spills were not harmful to the environment, and that increased monitoring had improved understanding of the sewer network.

BBC Scotland News has used the latest data to create an interactive map which you can use to find out how many spills were recorded in your area, and how long they lasted.

Sewage spills happen automatically at overflow sites, which are permitted to release excess water into natural waterways.

They usually consist of a pipe - set much higher than the usual water level - which provides an escape route when the system is deluged.

These overflows act as relief valves to prevent the sewer system from becoming overwhelmed during heavy rainfall and flooding into homes, businesses and streets.

The spills can last anywhere from a few minutes to hours.

Scottish Water currently has over 4,200 overflows across its network. The number of overflows with monitoring rose from 273 to 1,275 in 2024.

More than 100,000 spills totalling to almost 277,000 hours were recorded last year – an average of about 274 a day.

It is difficult to assess how the numbers compare to the previous year's figures, when 24,000 spills were recorded because of lower coverage.

The sites are all licensed to release untreated or partially-treated waste but just under 12% of overflows are legally required to report their data to the regulator, the Scottish Environment Protection Agency (Sepa).

Sepa said it has a "risk-based approach" which prioritises areas for monitoring based on population and environmental need.

However, none of the new monitors were required to be reported to Sepa.

Scottish Water figures show that Glasgow's River Clyde was one of the most impacted waterways in Scotland last year, receiving almost 6,150 spills - or the equivalent of 17 a day.

When adding in the Clyde Estuary, Firth of Clyde and other unnamed tributaries that run into the Clyde's waterways, this almost doubles to nearly 14,200, or 39 a day.

The Clyde Estuary also recorded the longest duration of spills - more than 25,000 hours - followed by the River Clyde with more than 15,000 hours.

Barcloy Mill Burn in Dumfries and Galloway, which is one of the newly-monitored sites, received the most spills last year, with a total of almost 3,500.

The data suggests that 225 sites recorded no spills and 525 recorded fewer than 10. There may also be errors which suggest a monitor is active when it is not.

There were 1,270 spills, totalling almost 1,500 hours, last year into West Lothian's River Almond, which is nearly 28 miles in length.

Local campaigner Ruth Plevin said swimming in the river was part of her childhood and that she now wants to protect it for her own grandchildren.

She said any investment in improving the infrastructure of the water system was welcome.

"It's what's not visible that is our concern - the microplastics, the pharmaceuticals, the agrichemicals, stuff that you can't see," she said.

Plevin, a member of the River Almond Action Group, said she wants the group's legacy to be clean, safe water.

"It's precious and I think we need to regard it as precious. Value it, look after it and make it safe.

"I want it to be clean - it's not a lot to ask for, really," she said.

Further along the east coast at Belhaven in East Lothian, surfer Brian Allen has been testing the local water for pollution.

Each week he sends samples to an accredited laboratory to be tested for E.coli and intestinal enterococci.

He says this is the same sampling as done by Sepa, except he tests all year round and not just during the bathing season.

Sepa monitors bathing water quality at about 80 sites across Scotland between May and September. It also looks out for algae, seaweed and waste.

Allen, the regional representative for Surfers Against Sewage, said the results had been providing "really good news" for Belhaven.

He said 86% of the samples were rated as excellent, good or sufficient water quality, which was fine for recreational water users.

"In fact 77% of the results are coming back as excellent. What we don't know is whether that picture is being replicated across the rest of Scotland," he said.

Allen welcomed Scottish Water's increase in data publishing and said working collaboratively would help build up a bigger picture of water quality.

He said the figures had showed there were almost daily discharges from the two overflows in the area – but it was not known if there was a link between discharges and water quality.

One of them, at West Barns at Dunbar, recorded 3,300 spills last year - the second highest number in Scotland last year and a newly-monitored site.

Simon Parsons, director for wastewater at Scottish Water, said most of the time overflows were doing the job they were designed for - draining rainwater out of the sewer system.

"The vast majority of those spills aren't harmful to the environment because they're nearly always about rainwater," he explained.

Scottish Water said 99% of spills were rainwater, surface water, road run-off, "grey" water from households (not human waste), infiltration of groundwater, and trade effluent.

Parsons said the increase in monitoring had improved understanding of the sewer network and helped identify locations requiring improvement.

"We didn't necessarily know how and when our overflows were operating so we've got a much better picture now than we've ever had before.

"We can actually identify those areas where we need to think about investment.

"We've got a number of locations across Scotland where actually we've identified links between how our pumps work and how our treatment works work, which have told us where we do get some spills when we shouldn't have them - and we'll make the improvements."

Monitoring in Scotland remains far lower than in England, which has 100% coverage .

Differences in recording means Scotland's figures are not directly comparable with the rest of the UK.

Scottish Water said its monitoring had now grown to about 50% and that it was aiming to reach 100% over the next five to six years.

Parsons said the cost was relatively small but represented good value in terms of the intelligence they provided.

articles.title: Monmouth flood victim died before she could return home
articles.summary: Jean Powell kept asking when she could go back to her flat, which was flooded when the River Monnow burst its banks.
articles.body:
When neighbours hammered on Jean Powell's door and evacuated her to safety because the nearby river had burst its banks and swamped her town, little did she know she would never return home.

Jean sought a 10-month refuge at her local Wetherspoons but kept asking when she could go back to her flat, which was flooded when the River Monnow hit 18-times its normal level in south Wales last November.

But the 95-year-old never got to go back home and died in September - one of those who suffered a personal toll from the effects of being flooded.

"Jean used to say, when am I going home?" said friend and neighbour Wyn Smith. "All she wanted to do was come back home and we couldn't fulfil that."

Jean was forced out of her home when the river hit record levels in the early hours of November 15 last year as a major incident was declared after almost a month's worth of rain fell in 24 hours.

It has been officially described as a one-in-75-year event when the river flooded more than 400 properties in Monmouth during Storm Claudia - and overwhelmed the defences that were built 35 years ago to protect the centre of town.

Jean, like many in the small town near the Wales and England border, was rescued and after sleeping the night on her neighbour's chair sought temporary sanctuary in Monmouth's Wetherspoons as she had no close family to look after her.

"She was happy in the beginning because she was in town where she wanted to be," recalled Wyn, who visited her friend staying in one of The Kings Head's hotel rooms most days.

"The Wetherspoons staff were brilliant with Jean, they'd take her food and really looked after her."

"We never thought she'd be there that long," said Wyn. "It's nobody's fault, it took a long time to dry her home out. It had to be done properly."

Residents have been with family, some are in rented accommodation, some have been in an Airbnb while another is in a care home.

Their story is typical of many in Monmouth who have been out of their home since Claudia struck - and that trauma and anxiety from the devastation of 12 months ago is never far from the surface.

"Some had been through the war and they said it upset them more than that. It was just awful," said Wyn.

"But unfortunately it could happen again. There's that fear. If they see water coming, it'll freak them out. They need to feel at home and not worry about the weather."

The Met Office estimates that with current levels of global warming, record-breaking wet winters have gone from once in 80-year events to once in 20-year events .

Wales' environmental body has warned long-range forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of wetter, windier weather than usual this winter with Natural Resources Wales (NRW) saying people should prepare for "the unthinkable" .

Apart from three nights at the local Premier Inn over Christmas when Wetherspoons was shut - where Jean had sandwiches from the nearby petrol station for Christmas dinner because she wanted to "remain independent" - she stayed above the pub in the town's main square for almost 10 months.

"As time went on, living in one room was awful for her," recalled Wyn, 70.

"When Jean got ill, it wasn't a place for her to live. Her health deteriorated and she didn't come back home, which is sad."

Jean's death will be acutely felt when the first displaced residents return to the Chippenham Court retirement complex she called home following its £1m refurbishment in the next few weeks.

One in seven properties in Wales are at risk of flooding, including the Frost household on the other side of Monmouth where Emily says she and her young family will never recover from being evacuated on a lifeboat last year.

The mum-of-two breaks down as she recalls being woken by the coastguard telling her she's got five minutes to evacuate her family as the floodwaters surge towards her end-of-terrace cottage.

"Opening the door, I completely freaked out to the lifeguard," Emily told the BBC.

"They were waist deep in water and said our house was at risk. I just needed to get our boys, who were then aged three and five, and they'd be back with a raft. We didn't have time to think about it."

What was supposed to be a night of celebration for her and husband Jake's 10th wedding anniversary, turned into a nightmare.

Emily and Jake didn't take their boys when they returned home the following day where more than a foot of water had penetrated their home.

"There was sludge and mud everywhere," she recalled.

"We didn't bring the boys home for a good while because we didn't want them seeing everything that they'd treasured had been destroyed.

"It was the toll it would take on them that worried us the most."

The Frosts lived in rental accommodation nearby for six months as they ripped out the downstairs of their home and started again.

Emily and Jake, who had also been flooded in 2020, have seen their boys "playing floods" so know their children have been "trying to process" their ordeal.

"They couldn't really understand why we weren't able to go home or have their things" said Emily.

"Because it's the time of year, even now when it rains they'll ask "are we staying home, is it okay? Luckily they're resilient as kids, but you still worry. People don't recover, it's something you'll just live with."

Environmental bodies estimate about 275,000 properties in Wales are at risk of flooding with another 400,000 in Scotland, while in England about 6.3 million properties - around 11.3m people - live in flood risk areas.

An official report said the River Monnow swelled to more than six-and-a-half metres after significant rainfall locally and upstream over the Black Mountains during a week where more than half-a-dozen Met Office rain warnings were issued.

Jennifer and Alan Morgan's 18th Century cottage near the banks of the Monnow had two more doors to hang after a five-year renovation when Claudia struck and they had to start it all again.

"I've not slept well for a year as it's been an absolutely living nightmare," said Jennifer, 70.

"The flooding was awful and the renovation has been so stressful, it's had a huge impact on us. We're not anywhere near to going back home, we probably won't be in until next summer.

"People might think because some of the shops and businesses are open that Monmouth is back to as it was before, but that's not the case - and we're proof."

The official Section 19 report into the flooding said flood warnings - where action is required as properties are in danger of flooding - were issued for all of Monmouth hours before the floods hit.

Wales' highest state of flood alert - the "risk to life and significant disruption" severe flood warning - was issued by NRW for the northern part of Monmouth on the Friday evening.

The severe flood warning for the rest of Monmouth was issued at 03:31 on the Saturday morning - but that was more than two hours after its flood defences were breached and after shops and homes had been flooded.

Emily had signed up to NRW's free flood alert service but went to bed because at midnight the rain had stopped and there was no water visible - half an hour before her young family were evacuated.

"When it stopped raining everyone probably thought 'oh well this has passed and we don't need to worry'," she said.

"Then the deluge of water just appeared from nowhere. It just shows how quickly it can change."

The official report recommended a review of the timing of severe flood warnings throughout the Monnow catchment "to ensure adequate advance notice is provided for people to respond effectively."

It also called for a review on the "uptake and understanding" of the flood warning service for those who live and work near the River Monnow.

NRW has said it reviews their "response, recovery and flood warning thresholds" after every serious incident to "identify lessons".

Of the one in seven properties in Wales classed as being at risk of flooding, NRW said less than a third of those eligible to receive flood warnings to their phone or email were currently signed up.

NRW argues Wales' geography makes it particularly vulnerable - with a vast coastline and "fast-responding" rivers which can fill at speed as rain runs off steep terrain in places like the south Wales valleys.

The official report also recommended a review into whether Monmouth town centre defences are fit for purpose.

"We're looking at our flood modelling and if there's anything else that can be done," said Sara Pearson of NRW.

"We're seeing flooding that we've never experienced before and with climate change that's set to increase. We can't prevent flooding, but we can help minimise the impact."

The Welsh Government has said it is spending almost £1.4m in flood risk management in Monmouthshire, including £700,000 of NRW funding for works at nearby Skenfrith.

"We have made £85m available this year to Natural Resources Wales and local authorities for flood and coastal erosion schemes across Wales," the government said in a statement.

NRW have said they've done work to clear rivers while the local council insist they've got more workers out clearing ditches, gullies and drains.

"We know how serious this is and how worrying it is for people," said Catrin Maby of Monmouthshire council.

"If it was only down to drain clearance we wouldn't need to worry. We need to look at the engineered defences again, we need to look at how we manage the land, we need to allocate sufficient resources into drainage and clearing those drains."

Insurance companies in the UK paid out £565 million to help homeowners recover from storms and floods in 2025 - and Emily's home is one of them with flood defence measures in place like flood gates and flood doors after advice from Flood Mary .

"I feel safer," added Emily. "I'll still be very apprehensive when you get the flood alert, it's whether you're gonna go back to that time or not.

"But you don't feel safe, which you should do in your own house."

articles.title: Oklahoma man executed for 2001 killing of girlfriend’s husband
articles.summary: McALESTER, Okla. — An Oklahoma man was put to death Thursday for the fatal shooting of his girlfriend’s estranged husband as he arrived to pick up his two young children before Thanksgiving.
articles.body: McALESTER, Okla. — An Oklahoma man was put to death Thursday for the fatal shooting of his girlfriend’s estranged husband as he arrived to pick up his two young children before Thanksgiving. It was the first in a pair of executions in the U.S. scheduled for Thursday. James Pavatt, 73, received a lethal injection at the state penitentiary in McAlester. His breathing did not appear labored during the execution, and he was declared unconscious about six minutes before being pronounced dead at 10:12 a.m. CT. In Texas, John Allen Rubio was set to be put to death Thursday evening. The 46-year-old was convicted of fatally stabbing and beheading three young children in 2003 in Brownsville, a border city with Mexico. Although the death penalty is getting renewed attention after the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee in September, the U.S. is on track to surpass 40 executions for a second consecutive year — a pace driven by Florida. Last week, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he would commute hundreds of death sentences before leaving office, which experts say would be the largest mass clemency in American history. On Thursday, former Oklahoma death row inmate Richard Glossip pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of being an accessory in a 1997 murder and awaits sentencing in December. Glossip, who had been on the brink of execution three times, was released on bond in May after spending nearly 30 years in prison. The U.S. Supreme Court had overturned his conviction and he was awaiting a retrial. Oklahoma advertising executive killed in garage When Pavatt was asked if he had any last words, he shook his head no. As a chaplain read to him from a Bible, he appeared to be mouthing some words, but they could not be heard. Pavatt was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in the 2001 death of Rob Andrew, a 39-year-old advertising executive. Pavatt attended the same church as the Andrew family and had been having an affair with Rob Andrew’s wife, Brenda Andrew. She was convicted at a separate trial and is currently the only woman on death row in Oklahoma. Weeks before the shooting, Rob Andrew told police someone was trying to kill him after the brake lines on his car were cut. Brenda Andrew told police after her husband was killed that masked intruders shot her in the arm and fatally shot him. Pavatt and Brenda Andrew went to Mexico with her two children after the shooting and were arrested three months later while reentering the U.S. At a clemency hearing last month, Pavatt said he was “not guilty of shooting anyone,” and that he’d fallen in love with Brenda Andrew and believed “everything she told me.” “It was not until my trial that I began to see the extent to which I had been manipulated by Brenda,” Pavatt told the board. “I can see why the jury believed that we were both involved in Rob’s murder.” Prosecutors have said that Pavatt and Brenda Andrew plotted to kill her husband, and that no matter who fired the shots, both were equally guilty. No family members of Rob Andrew or Pavatt witnessed the execution, although his daughter and her husband visited him the night before, a prison spokesperson said. 3 young children beheaded in Texas Rubio and his girlfriend, Angela Camacho, were accused in the killings of 3-year-old Julissa Quesada, 14-month-old John E. Rubio and 2-month-old Mary Jane Rubio in the squalid, windowless apartment they shared in Brownsville, located on Texas’ border with Mexico. Camacho pleaded guilty and is serving a life sentence. Rubio’s first capital murder conviction in the killings was overturned by an appeals court, which ruled that statements by Camacho were wrongly allowed as evidence in his trial. Rubio again pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity for his second trial but he was once again convicted and sentenced to death. Rubio, according to court records, wasn’t the biological father of the two older children but treated them as if they were his own. At various points, Rubio claimed the children were possessed and that he was the “chosen one” intended to save the world. Defense experts diagnosed Rubio as suffering from paranoid schizophrenia, a determination rejected by prosecution experts. Defense experts testified his childhood — filled with violence at home, “toxic” parents, drug use and prostitution — damaged him developmentally. The apartment building where the children were killed was later demolished and the land was turned into a park and a community garden. Rubio was set to be executed Thursday evening at the state prison in Huntsville.

articles.title: Former owner of Peanut the squirrel, viral pet euthanized by NY officials, detained by ICE
articles.summary: Nearly two years after New York officials euthanized Peanut the squirrel, his former owners face another ordeal as Daniela Bittner remains in ICE custody.
articles.body: The wife of the New York man whose viral pet squirrel Peanut was seized and euthanized by wildlife officials in 2024 has been detained by immigration authorities. Daniela Bittner, a German native, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in mid-October at a small airport near New York's border with Pennsylvania, according to The Associated Press (AP). She and her husband of four years, Mark Longo, were planning to attend a TikTok event when officers approached them, according to the New York Post. Longo said his wife's detention stemmed from what he described as a minor paperwork issue, The AP said. The couple reportedly made an error on one of her immigration forms and failed to catch it while dealing with the seizure and euthanasia of Peanut. OWNERS OF BELOVED PEANUT THE SQUIRREL PLAN TO SUE NEW YORK STATE OVER SEIZURE AND KILLING BY AUTHORITIES "She came into this country legally on a visa. We filed the paperwork and stuff and apparently the government is saying we filed the wrong piece of paper," Longo told The Post. "They had asked for additional information, which we provided, and then apparently they sent a letter stating that it was denied because we filed the wrong paperwork, which we never received," he said. "This is a minor paperwork issue and it’s being treated as if my wife literally crawled out a hole to get into this country," he added. PEANUT THE PET SQUIRREL TAKEN AWAY BY NEW YORK STATE OFFICIALS FROM ADOPTED HOME, MAY BE EUTHANIZED Longo said Bittner has no criminal history and was hit with the maximum penalty, potentially facing deportation without a hearing, according to The Post. The couple reportedly married in 2022, shortly after Bittner returned to Germany to resolve a visa situation. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) told the outlet that Bittner lawfully entered the U.S. multiple times between May 2021 and November 2022, each time receiving permission to stay for a temporary period. However, DHS said she was arrested because she "chose to overstay her welcome in defiance of our nation's laws." "To be clear, a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States," DHS told the Post. Bittner has reportedly been transferred between several detention centers, from Syracuse to Buffalo, Louisiana and eventually Texas. Longo described the conditions his wife has faced in federal custody as "deplorable," The AP said. Her arrest has also cast uncertainty over the couple's nonprofit animal rescue operation, where Bittner reportedly cares for 600 animals rescued from neglect. "If my wife gets deported for a paperwork issue, we will lose EVERYTHING we worked for. Our Nonprofit Animal Sanctuary will close and 600 animals will have to find another home. All we wanted was to be left alone. We finally moved on from the tragic murder of P'Nut, now to this," he said.
